reason: The mapping to Art. 13 and Art. 25(4) of the EU AI Act provides a defensible basis. Art. 13 requires providers to maintain documentation, which includes an inventory of components and subcontractors. Art. 25(4) mandates that providers ensure subcontractors comply with the Act, which necessitates tracking them. Together, these provisions support the control objective of maintaining an inventory.
applicability_note: This control is specifically applicable to AI systems that use third-party components, as the Act's obligations for documentation and subcontractor management are triggered in such supply chain contexts.
challenge_comment: The challenge lies in the practical implementation of maintaining a comprehensive and up-to-date inventory, especially for complex AI systems with numerous components and dynamic subcontractor relationships.
